variables.name: BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR

readers.program: bash -c child command started by bin/ci/test-background-check.sh
readers.mechanism: shell expansion inside the text of a bash -c command

setters.value: a new directory made by mktemp -d (assigned on line 7)
setters.why: gives the test its own state root, separate from the CI job that hosts it
makes background-check.sh fall back to RUNNER_TEMP for the reused-runner case

variables.values: Path to a directory. The text is used as given.
variables.default: Unset or empty: the state root is RUNNER_TEMP. If RUNNER_TEMP is unset or empty, it is TMPDIR. If TMPDIR is unset or empty, it is /tmp.
variables.effect: Sets the root directory where background-check.sh keeps the state of each background check (started, log, pid, status and finished files) under background-check-<NAME>. When GITHUB_RUN_ID is set, the script first appends background-checks-<run id>-<attempt>-<job> to the root.
variables.notes: No workflow sets it. gcp-nix.yml lines 73 and 116 call the script without it, so the state root there is RUNNER_TEMP. bin/ci/README.md lines 328 to 331 say that matrix jobs which share a temp directory must supply separate BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR roots.

variables.name: RUNNER_TEMP

setters.why: simulates the temp directory of a reused runner

variables.values: Path to a directory. The text is used as given.
variables.default: background-check.sh and resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh: unset or empty falls back to TMPDIR, then to /tmp. bench-refresh-ci.sh (derive-publication, upsert-pr, reconcile-health): unset or empty stops the script with the message 'RUNNER_TEMP is required'.
variables.effect: bench-refresh-ci.sh writes its work files there: publication-base.json, publication-apply-state.txt, bench-refresh-pr.md and bench-refresh-health-alert.md. background-check.sh uses it as the state root when BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR is not set. resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh puts the nix out-link perfetto-host-binaries-<uid> there.
variables.notes: The GitHub Actions runner provides it. bench-refresh-ci.sh also reads it on line 442. The workflows pass further paths under $RUNNER_TEMP as script arguments.

variables.name: TMPDIR
variables.values: Path to a directory. The text is used as given.
variables.default: Unset or empty: /tmp.
variables.effect: Second fallback for the state root of background-check.sh and for the directory of the nix out-link in resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh. It is used only when RUNNER_TEMP (and, in background-check.sh, BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR) is unset or empty.
variables.notes: Many scripts of this area call mktemp without naming a directory, for example ci-bundle-artifact.sh line 38 and test/deb-package-contents.sh lines 35 to 38. GNU mktemp then creates the file under TMPDIR, or under /tmp when TMPDIR is unset. That is mktemp behaviour, measured with GNU coreutils 8.32 outside the checkout. No script names TMPDIR for it. ci-shared-nfs.sh always gives mktemp a full path, so TMPDIR has no effect there.

variables.name: SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
variables.values: Whole number of seconds from 60 to 5400, written with 2 to 5 digits. Any other non-empty text stops the script with 'measurement timeout override must be between 60 and 5400 seconds' and exit status 1.
variables.default: Unset or empty: the measurement budget is 5400 seconds (90 minutes).
variables.effect: Replaces the 5400 second budget that run-measurement gives to the 'bin/slice submit' measurement command through timeout. On a scheduled run the budget is still cut to the time left before SLICE_REFRESH_STOP_UTC minus 30 seconds.
variables.notes: .github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml line 119 sets it from the workflow_dispatch input measurement_timeout_seconds. The validate-invocation sub-command accepts the same override as an argument only for a dispatched dry run. A final budget below 60 seconds stops the script with exit status 1.

variables.name: GITHUB_EVENT_NAME

setters.value: the event name of each test case (push, workflow_dispatch, schedule, pull_request)
setters.why: drives the resolver through its cases

variables.values: Event name text. bench-refresh-ci.sh compares it with exactly 'schedule'. resolve-apt-channel.sh compares it with exactly 'workflow_dispatch'.
variables.default: Unset or empty: bench-refresh-ci.sh applies no stop-time limit. resolve-apt-channel.sh ignores DISPATCH_CHANNEL.
variables.effect: bench-refresh-ci.sh: on a 'schedule' event the measurement budget is cut. The cut makes the run end 30 seconds before SLICE_REFRESH_STOP_UTC. resolve-apt-channel.sh: on a 'workflow_dispatch' event a non-empty DISPATCH_CHANNEL selects the apt channel.
variables.notes: The GitHub Actions runner provides it. bench-refresh.yml also passes the same value to validate-invocation as an argument.

variables.name: SLICE_REFRESH_STOP_UTC
variables.values: A time of day in UTC, for example 06:30:00. The text is handed to 'date -u -d "<today> <value> UTC"' and is not checked by the script.
variables.default: Unset or empty: 06:30:00 UTC.
variables.effect: Read only when GITHUB_EVENT_NAME is 'schedule'. The measurement budget becomes the smaller of the normal budget and (stop time - now - 30 seconds). If less than 60 seconds remain, the script stops with 'refresh deadline leaves less than 60 seconds for measurement'.
variables.notes: .github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml line 42 sets it to "06:30:00" for the whole workflow. The stop time is taken on the UTC day of the start time.
